metadata.dataset_context: 2017/18 football season; initial curated reference set, not an exhaustive manager register
metadata.purpose: Provide research-derived tactical context alongside Wyscout event-derived team and player metrics.
metadata.interpretation: These are qualitative, season-scoped reference notes. They are not model predictions, fixed personality traits, or proof that a team used one style in every match.

profiles.qualitative_summary: A positional-play approach built around controlled possession, central numerical advantages and structured rest defence. The team's shape could change between build-up and attacking phases.
Associated with aggressive pressing and rapid attacking transitions after regaining possession. Treat these as tendencies to test against the season's event data, not assumptions about every match.
profiles.evidence_type: published season tactical review plus established coaching profile

profiles.qualitative_summary: Arsenal used multiple shapes during the season, including a prominent back-three structure at times. Do not reduce the season to a single formation or one fixed tactical label.

The 3-4-2-1 was a prominent back-three system associated with Conte in the Premier League's 2017/18 tactical review. Chelsea also used other shapes; this is a reference tendency, not a match-level label.

The Premier League review identifies Burnley among the teams with the fewest starting formations and notes Dyche retained a traditional back four throughout the season. Other style tags should be validated against event data before being scored.
